en: The southwest monsoon, locally called Habagat, brings heavy rainfall to the Philippines between June and September.
Soil near Mayon Volcano is highly fertile because volcanic ash adds rich minerals to the earth.
Romblon province produces high-quality marble, a metamorphic rock formed from limestone under intense heat and pressure.
When water vapor cools in the high altitudes of Baguio, it condenses into visible clouds or fog.
Because the Philippines lies near the equator, we experience roughly twelve hours of daylight every day.
The three bright stars forming Orion's Belt, locally called Balatik, are easily visible in the night sky.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the ocean water in Manila Bay to rise and fall.
PAGASA issues Signal Number One when a tropical cyclone brings winds of 39 to 61 kilometers per hour.
During a local thunderstorm, you see lightning before hearing thunder because light travels faster than sound.
Heavy rains on the steep slopes of the Cordillera mountains can cause soil erosion and dangerous landslides.
River rocks in the Chico River become smooth and round because flowing water constantly tumbles them together.
The Philippines experiences frequent earthquakes because it is located along the highly active Pacific Ring of Fire.
